title: Breeding programmes are being repackaged as named, branded platforms rather than sold as individual cultivars
observation: Within the observation window three separate breeders moved blueberry genetics behind a named platform rather than a cultivar list: Costa launched BluGenix on 29 May 2026 as the brand and platform for its breeding programme, introduced with five varieties at once; Fall Creek operates the closed SEKOYA member platform alongside the Fall Creek Collection and an open catalogue; and United Exports commercialises the Mazzardis 'EB'/'NS' selections under the single OZblu brand rather than under their patent denominations.
why_it_might_matter: If genetics is increasingly sold as platform membership rather than per-variety licence, the competitive unit shifts from cultivar performance to platform terms - access, exclusivity, royalty structure and marketing support. Variety-level tracking alone would then under-describe the market.
what_would_confirm_it: Published platform membership terms, royalty structures or member rosters for two or more of these platforms; or evidence that growers select between platforms rather than between cultivars.
what_would_falsify_it: Evidence that these platforms are marketing wrappers over conventional per-variety licences with no distinct commercial terms; or platform dissolution or reversion to open catalogue sales.
